avoid.product_type: Apple-branded products (AirPods, AirTag, Apple Watch, iPad, EarPods)
avoid.reason: Heavily brand-locked — cannot be legally dropshipped, Apple MAP pricing agreements eliminate any margin, and counterfeit risk creates platform bans; these products signal category demand only, not dropship opportunities.

avoid.product_type: Large-screen Smart TVs (55-inch+ 4K Fire TV / LED TVs)
avoid.reason: Oversized and extremely heavy freight costs destroy all margin — a 55-inch TV requires freight shipping that often costs $100–$200+, return rates are high, and the category is dominated by big-box retail pricing power that generic sellers cannot compete with.

avoid.product_type: Amazon-branded subscription services (Blink Plus Plan, Alexa+, Echo ecosystem lock-in products)
avoid.reason: These are Amazon's own proprietary subscription products tied to their ecosystem — no resell pathway exists, and trying to compete with Amazon's own branded hardware/software products on Amazon is a losing strategy for dropshippers.

avoid.product_type: Amazon Kindle e-readers (Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle hardware)
avoid.reason: Amazon's own branded hardware with razor-thin authorized reseller margins — the platform actively prices these at cost to drive Kindle Unlimited subscriptions, making it impossible for dropshippers to compete on price or positioning.

avoid.product_type: Branded beats/JBL headphone exact replicas (counterfeit-adjacent listings)
avoid.reason: Attempting to ride the Beats or JBL brand wave with near-replica products creates serious IP infringement risk, platform delisting, and potential legal liability — target the category with clearly generic-branded alternatives instead.

analysis.market_insights:
It is Black Friday 2026, the single most important 72-hour window in annual e-commerce. The Amazon data paints an unusually clear picture: this Q4 is defined by three convergent mega-trends — wearable health tech (smart rings), wireless audio (earbuds and headphones dominating electronics), and cozy comfort home goods (drinkware, blankets, bedding). The absence of TikTok-specific data in today's feed is a limitation, but Amazon signal alone is actionable: when five audio products, two drinkware items, and two sheet sets all simultaneously appear in category top 10s, the category-level demand is confirmed. Dropshippers should focus on lightweight, non-branded alternatives in these exact categories and move sourcing decisions TODAY — the holiday buying window runs approximately 3 more weeks before post-Christmas demand softens.

Looking 4–8 weeks forward, the smart money is positioning for the January wellness and home-reset supercycle. Resistance bands, posture correctors, meal prep containers, LED room lighting, and weighted blankets all have highly predictable January demand spikes tied to New Year resolutions, and smart dropshippers use the revenue from Q4 gifting sales to fund January inventory positioning now. The smart ring category deserves special attention: the Oura Ring 5 Sizing Kit appearing as a standalone Amazon bestseller is an unusually strong early-adopter signal — when consumers are buying sizing kits as a step toward purchasing a $400+ ring, it confirms the category is entering mass-market adoption. Generic smart rings with sleep and heart rate features in the $30–$70 range are positioned for a multi-month demand cycle through early 2027.
